representation.dense_surface: compose_index_text({title, site_name, body}) = "<title>. <site_name>. <body>" with a head token skipped when the body already has it (cytir.core.common.compose_index_text). `body` is the passage's `dense_text` when the chunker emits one, else its `text` (cytir.core.common.record_text_channels).
representation.sparse_surface: the same compose_index_text composition over the passage's `sparse_text` when present, else `text` (record_text_channels fallback); BM25 leg only. For chunk@1 text the two channels are identical; the epoch-4 structured chunker may emit a channel pair (cytir.core.common.passage_from_chunk).
representation.ruling_cite: decisions.md ADR-061 (2026-07-18): title + site_name belong in BOTH retrieval vectors on every content chunk (`aw_common.compose_index_text`, called at embed). The web-page family path (cytir.sources.families.web -> cytir.core.common.process_html -> passage) is the code that ADR names. representation.sparse_surface: the same compose_index_text composition over the passage's `sparse_text` when present, else `text` (record_text_channels fallback); BM25 leg only. consent.basis: EXPLICIT GRANT via the publisher's own data dump, per Tim's ruling 2026-09-22 (verbatim: "Use the dump licence as consent for Stack Exchange"). These rows come from the OFFICIAL Stack Exchange data dump, which Stack Exchange itself publishes with a per-post CC BY-SA licence -- not from crawling stackoverflow.com. ADR-103 rules that consent governs FETCH; there is no fetch of the site here to govern, and the publisher's own act of distributing the corpus under a licence that permits redistribution IS the grant. `explicit-grant` is therefore the accurate value in the ratified vocabulary rather than a workaround for it: it is the same slot de_openlegaldata_v1 (task 459/489, on main) uses for its dump route, and it is what consent_resolver.bucket's EXCEPTION 1 means by an explicit grant -- a publisher act, as opposed to the absence-of-objection that `live-per-origin` reads out of robots. It differs from de_openlegaldata_v1 in ONE respect worth naming: that family's robots.txt invites the dump route in words, whereas stackoverflow.com's robots.txt is unreadable (418, below). The grant here is carried by the dump instrument alone, not by a robots invitation.
evidence: The probe that is NOT the gate, kept because it is what was measured: stackoverflow.com/robots.txt returns HTTP 418 with an empty body, confirmed across two independent fetches from heimdall (task 629 P7, tasks/629-artifacts/pool-a-consent.v1.json). consent_resolver's robots_unreadable_class classifies 418 as unreadable -- not in the readable-open {200,404,410} set -- so under a crawl-route reading the terminal failed closed to held/consent_unreadable. That reading is superseded for this family by the ruling above, and the 418 is retained here so nobody concludes the signal was readable.

Licence, independently: the dump carries a per-post licence read from the instrument itself (CC BY-SA 3.0 for the question, 2.5 for the accepted answer on the sampled tranche) -- tasks/629-artifacts/pool-a-licence.v1.json. Consent and licence remain independent gates (100M spec 7.1 guard 6); the licence does not stand in for consent, the DUMP ROUTE does.

declared_payload.basis: POLICY 4.4's VENDOR-CONTENT CLASS, ratified by Tim (D1, 2026-07-27) after the wave-2/tier-1 vendor-SEO flood, applied to rows that match its definition verbatim. 4.4: "Commercial-vendor content that is not [canonical documentation] -- vendor engineering blogs, product marketing, glossary/checklist/SEO surfaces, and vendor tool listings -- carries the dedicated vendor-content trust class (trust_tier = 0.60), below the technical-documentation default (0.75), regardless of content quality or title-match strength." These rows are `sunfounder.com/products/...`-shaped product pages on commercial vendor hosts: not a docs subdomain, not a /docs/-class path, so 4.4's keep-rule for "genuine product documentation" does not reach them. 4.4's standing rule points the same way for anything left ambiguous: absent affirmative classification as canonical documentation, a host "enters at the vendor-content class (0.60) or below". NOT a new policy value -- the ratified one, applied.
declared_payload.source_type_basis: `docs` is what the vendor-content class ACTUALLY CARRIES in the index, read from the implementation rather than chosen: task 330 implemented D1 on the build collection and its restamp wrote `{"trust_tier": 0.60}` and NOTHING ELSE (tasks/330-scripts/restamp330_trust.py:118), over a cohort whose predicate REQUIRES `source_type = docs`. All 765,014 points at class@0.60 therefore carry source_type=docs. And `tech` is not a source_type at all: it is a `disc_class`, which `pipeline/discovery_ingest.py`'s CLASS_SOURCE maps TO `docs` -- as it maps `commercial` and `other` as well. The vocabulary offers exactly three values (official / reference / docs) and no product or vendor one, so `docs` is not a compromise here, it is the only value the serving vocabulary has for this class. Inventing a fourth for 445 points would create a ranking class with no learned weight. CORRECTION, task 629 2026-09-23 (coordinator's ruling): the sentence above -- "The vocabulary offers exactly three values (official / reference / docs)" -- is FALSE of the index, and true only of `discovery_ingest.CLASS_SOURCE`'s map. Measured on the aw_e8 twin: `statcan.gc.ca` serves 10,200 rows at source_type `gov-stat` (plus 94 at the mis-spelling `gov-stats`, a defect of that family), stamped by pipeline/ingest_statcan_wds.py:183. Every ingester stamps its own hosts (aw_serving_metadata.py:63), so the serving vocabulary is the union of two dozen ingesters' constants and cannot be read off one map. The CHOICE of `docs` for this family is unaffected -- `gov-stat` is a statistics-agency class and B01 is vendor product pages -- but the argument that `docs` was the ONLY available value was not sound.
